purpose: Synthetic paired target sampling, strict complete-event history, target-logit loss, gradients, microbatch update boundaries and saved-result identity acceptance
checks: Artificial CSV fold isolation, complete-query/history eligibility, boundary partials and discarded tails
Stateless paired sampling with replacement, repeated draws, weights and no global RNG consumption
KC200 complete suffix, same targets and external labels across paired histories
Actual classifier logits agree with original-forward observation, extreme-logit BCE stability
Current/future response isolation, permitted-history positive control, effective matching parameter gradients
Whole-batch weighted normalization with multiple microbatches and unchanged default engine branch
Inert engine objects verify one step per chunk batch and no step after incomplete/failed microbatches
Explicit config/checkpoint/metadata/saved-prediction training identity and existing pure-file reader regression
static_review: Root and independent frontier_audit reviewed the final executable changes before freezing this check; no blocking finding remains.
limitations: Synthetic CPU checks do not establish actual training speed, validation gains or scientific novelty.
Only explicit KTST mean shared-development fold0 recipes are supported in this first adaptation.
Sampling changes supervision coverage and variance; negative low-coverage results are not a full-supervision falsification.
No real training batch, backbone or K is selected by this acceptance record.
A future NIPS pilot also needs an original full-supervision anchor and comparisons against stronger completed baselines.
The frozen final-test evaluator does not automatically support this training identity.
